look_here_first: The leaves look silver because they are densely covered with appressed silky hairs. Plants are low, wiry perennials with narrow gray-green leaves and purple-rayed heads.

project_inclusion.range_basis: County-level Texas distribution sources document Hays, Travis, and Comal; UT also documents the species in Williamson County.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Only counties explicitly listed in specimen/flora-derived sources are counted.

best_field_traits: dense appressed silky hairs giving silver-gray appearance
purple ray florets around yellow disc florets
heads usually solitary on branch tips
morphology_keys.comparison_training: The silver-sericeous foliage is the fastest split from S. patens, S. oblongifolium, and S. ericoides.
